issues.legal_issue: A purchaser’s covenant to discharge an encumbrance on property sold creates an implied contract of indemnity in favour of the vendor.
material_facts: The sale deed concerned property subject to an existing mortgage and left part of the purchase consideration with the purchasers to pay the mortgage debt.
The purchasers failed to pay the mortgagees.
issues.conclusion: The covenant to pay off the mortgage was also an implied undertaking to indemnify the vendors against loss resulting from its non-performance. The vendors had a distinct claim for indemnity if that failure caused them actual loss.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 124 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, indemnity is a promise to save another from loss caused by the promisor or another person. A covenant by a purchaser to pay an encumbrance is an implied contract of indemnity. The court relied on Musammat Izzat-un-Nissa Begam v. Kunwar Pertab Singh and the Full Bench decision in Tilak Ram v. Surat Singh. It also distinguished the vendor’s action to be placed in a position to meet the liability, for which limitation runs from when the purchaser ought to have paid, from an indemnity action based on loss actually incurred.

rule.if: indemnity_contract_appeal and property_sold_subject_to_encumbrance and purchaser_promised_to_discharge_encumbrance and purchaser_failed_to_discharge_encumbrance

predicates.indemnity_contract_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a claim for indemnity arising from a contractual undertaking.
predicates.property_sold_subject_to_encumbrance: A vendor sold property that was subject to an existing encumbrance.
predicates.purchaser_promised_to_discharge_encumbra: The purchaser undertook to pay off the encumbrance on the property.
predicates.purchaser_failed_to_discharge_encumbranc: The purchaser did not pay off the encumbrance as undertaken.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an indemnity claim and the purchaser of encumbered property undertook but failed to discharge the encumbrance, the rule treats an implied indemnity contract as existing.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for loss under an implied indemnity arising from a covenant in a registered conveyance is governed by the limitation provisions applicable to indemnity contracts and registered instruments.
material_facts: The covenant to pay the mortgage debt was contained in a registered sale deed.
The vendors sued to recover the loss they said resulted from the purchasers’ failure to discharge the mortgage.
issues.conclusion: Article 83 applied to the implied contract of indemnity, and Article 116 gave the vendors six years to sue because the sale deed was registered.
issues.legal_principle: Article 83 of the Limitation Act, 1908 applies to suits on express and implied contracts of indemnity. Read with Article 116, it allowed six years for a suit founded on the registered sale deed. The court relied on Musammat Izzat-un-Nissa Begam v. Kunwar Pertab Singh, Tilak Ram v. Surat Singh, and the authorities cited there, including Kumar Nath Bhuttacharjee v. Nobo Kumar Bhuttacharjee, Ratan Bai v. Ghasiram Gangabisan Wani, Harakchand Tarachand v. Sumatilal Chunilal, Gulabrao Vithoba v. Shamrao Jagoba, Naima Khatun v. Sardar Basant Singh, Ram Barai Singh v. Sheodeni Singh, and Venkatanarayaniah v. Subramania Iyer.

predicates.indemnity_limitation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal disputing the limitation period for an indemnity claim.
predicates.seller_sued_on_indemnity_contract: A seller brought suit to recover loss under an indemnity undertaking made by the purchaser.
predicates.indemnity_contract_arose_from_registered: The indemnity undertaking arose from a registered conveyance.

issues.definition: When a limitation appeal concerns a seller’s indemnity suit founded on an undertaking in a registered conveyance, the rule applies the limitation period for a registered contract to the claim.

issues.legal_issue: Limitation on a vendor’s indemnity claim begins when the vendor actually suffers loss, not merely when a decree is entered against the vendor.
material_facts: A final mortgage decree was passed against the vendors in 1937.
In 1943, proceedings to liquidate the debt required the vendors to execute a self-liquidating mortgage over part of their property and deliver possession of that share to the mortgagees.
The vendors filed suit after being compelled to execute that mortgage and deliver possession, and the suit was within six years of that loss.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage decree alone did not start limitation. The vendors were actually damnified when compelled to execute the self-liquidating mortgage in 1943, so their suit was within time.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 83 of the Limitation Act, 1908, time on an indemnity claim runs from actual damnification; the event giving rise to a risk of loss or a decree against the claimant is not by itself sufficient. The court relied on Collinge v. Heywood and the statement in 1 Williams’ Saunders 117, note 1, that a claim under an undertaking to indemnify or save harmless cannot be brought until loss has arisen.

rule.if: indemnity_limitation_appeal and seller_sued_on_indemnity_contract and decree_preceded_actual_loss and seller_suffered_actual_loss and suit_filed_within_applicable_limitation_window

predicates.indemnity_limitation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal disputing limitation on an indemnity claim.
predicates.seller_sued_on_indemnity_contract: A seller brought suit for loss under a purchaser’s indemnity undertaking.
predicates.decree_preceded_actual_loss: A decree was entered against the seller before the seller actually suffered the loss claimed.
predicates.seller_suffered_actual_loss: The seller later incurred actual loss as a result of the purchaser’s failure to discharge the encumbrance.
predicates.suit_filed_within_applicable_limitation_: The seller filed suit within the applicable limitation period measured from the actual loss.

issues.definition: When a decree against a seller precedes actual loss under an indemnity undertaking, the rule measures limitation from the later actual loss and treats a suit filed within the applicable window as timely.
